subject: URGENT!!! Your Account Will Be BLOCKED In 24 Hours
body:
Dear Valued Costumer,

We noticed unusual activity on your account. Your account will be BLOCKED within 24 hours unless you verify your details.

Click below and enter your BVN, ATM card number and 4-digit PIN to keep your account active:

Verify My Account Now

Failure to comply will result in permanent closure.

GTBank Security Team

red_flags.description: A bank writing from a free @gmail.com address
Threat of account closure within 24 hours
Asks for your card PIN and BVN, which no bank ever requests
red_flags.spot: BVN, ATM card number and 4-digit PIN

red_flags.description: Spelling mistake: "Costumer"
Link goes to gtb-verify-account.xyz, not gtbank.com

explanation: Banks never ask for your PIN or BVN by email. Urgency, a Gmail sender and a strange link are the classic signs of a banking phish.

subject: CONGRATULATIONS!!! You Have Won ₦5,000,000
body:
Congratulations!

Your phone number was randomly selected as a WINNER in the MTN Mega Anniversary Promo. You have won ₦5,000,000 (Five Million Naira).

Account: 0123456789 | Bank: Opay | Name: Promo Claims Office

Offer expires TODAY.

red_flags.description: You won a promo you never entered
red_flags.spot: Your phone number was randomly selected

red_flags.description: You must pay a "processing fee" to receive a prize
Payment goes to a personal account, not MTN
Sent from a free Outlook address
"Expires TODAY" pressure

explanation: Real prizes never require you to pay to receive them. This is advance-fee fraud dressed up as a promo.

subject: Federal Government Youth Grant ₦250,000 Approved For You
body:
Good day,

You have been approved for the Federal Government Youth Empowerment Grant of ₦250,000.

To receive payment, reply to this email with:
- Full name

- Bank account number
- Date of birth

Central Bank of Nigeria

red_flags.description: Government agency using a Yahoo address
Asks for NIN, BVN and bank details by email reply
You never applied for a grant
"Do not share this message" secrecy

explanation: Government bodies do not collect your NIN or BVN by email reply, and they do not write from Yahoo or Gmail. Free money plus a request for your ID numbers means identity theft.

subject: You Won an iPhone 15 Pro Max – Pay Delivery Only!
body:
JUMIA

Hello Lucky Customer!!!

You are our 1,000,000th visitor and you have won a brand new iPhone 15 Pro Max!

Just pay ₦4,500 for delivery and your phone will arrive in 2 days.

CLAIM MY IPHONE

red_flags.description: "1,000,000th visitor" prize is a well-known scam line
Domain jumia-free-gifts.net is not jumia.com.ng
Pay a small fee to receive an expensive prize
Fake scarcity: "Only 3 phones left!"

explanation: A free expensive gift that only needs a small payment is bait. The real Jumia emails from jumia.com.ng.

subject: Your payment was declined – update now
body:
NETFLIX

Dear Costumer,

We was unable to process your last payment. Your Netflix membership will be cancel today.

Please update your card details to continue enjoying Netflix:

Update Payment

Netflix Team

red_flags.description: Misspelled domain: netflx-support.com (missing the "i")
Bad grammar: "We was unable", "will be cancel"
Cancellation today unless you act
Asks you to enter card details through a link

explanation: Typosquatted domains like "netflx" are cheap to register. If billing is really a problem, open the Netflix app directly.

subject: Work From Home – Earn $500 Daily, No Experience
body:
Hello,

Shell Nigeria is hiring online workers. No interview, no experience. Earn $500 per day from your phone!

To secure your slot, pay a registration fee of ₦10,000 and message our HR manager on WhatsApp: +234 801 234 5678.

red_flags.description: Big multinational recruiting from a Gmail address
Unrealistic pay with no interview or experience
red_flags.spot: Earn $500 per day from your phone!

red_flags.description: Registration fee to get a job
Moves you to WhatsApp, away from official channels
red_flags.spot: message our HR manager on WhatsApp

explanation: Legitimate employers never charge you to apply. Job scams target students and graduates with easy-money promises.

subject: Mailbox Full – You Will Stop Receiving Emails
body:
Your mailbox has exceeded its storage limit (99.8%).

You will stop receiving new messages and old messages will be DELETED.

Click below and log in with your email password to upgrade your storage for free:

Upgrade Storage

System Administrator

red_flags.description: Generic "Mail Administrator" from an unrelated domain
Threat that your emails will be deleted
Asks you to log in through a link to "upgrade"
red_flags.spot: log in with your email password

red_flags.description: No company name, logo or contact

explanation: Fake "mailbox full" notices are a classic way to steal email passwords. Your real email provider shows storage warnings inside the app.

subject: STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL: Inheritance Fund of $8.5 Million
body:
Dear Friend,

I am Barrister James Williams, personal lawyer to the late Mr. Robert Okafor who died in a plane crash with his family. He left $8,500,000 USD in a bank with no next of kin. Since you share the same surname, I want to present you as the beneficiary.

We will share the money 50/50. Kindly send your full name, phone number and a copy of your ID card to begin the transfer.

This transaction is 100% risk free.

Yours faithfully,
Barr. James Williams

red_flags.description: A stranger offering you millions
Asks you to pose as a fake next of kin
Requests ID card and personal details
red_flags.spot: a copy of your ID card

red_flags.description: "100% risk free" and "strictly confidential"

explanation: This is the classic 419 scam. Once you reply, "fees" and "taxes" follow until you stop paying.

subject: Your package is on hold – pay customs fee
body:
DHL Express

Dear customer,

Your package could not be delivered because customs duty of ₦3,500 has not been paid.

Pay now to avoid your package being returned to sender:

Pay Customs Fee

DHL Express Nigeria

red_flags.description: You were not expecting a package
red_flags.spot: Your package could not be delivered

red_flags.description: Domain dhl-parcels-ng.com is not dhl.com
Shortened bit.ly link hides the destination
Small fee request designed not to feel risky

explanation: Fake delivery fees are one of the most common scams. Track parcels yourself on the courier's official site using your tracking number.

subject: Upgrade Your JAMB Score Before Admission List
body:
Attention Candidate,

We can officially upgrade your UTME score to 300+ before the admission list is released.

Pay ₦20,000 and send your registration number and phone number. 100% guaranteed.

Don't miss this chance!

red_flags.description: Offers something impossible: changing an exam score
JAMB using a Gmail address
Asks for payment and your registration number
red_flags.spot: Pay ₦20,000 and send your registration number

red_flags.description: "100% guaranteed" promise

explanation: Score upgrades do not exist. JAMB uses jamb.gov.ng, and offers like this exist only to take your money.

Tells you to use the app, no link to log in
trust_signals.spot: in the Jumia app under My Orders

subject: Your Friday evening trip with Uber
body:

subject: Welcome to Google Cybersecurity Certificate
body:
coursera

Hi Ada,

The Coursera Team

trust_signals.description: Sender subdomain belongs to coursera.org
Link goes to coursera.org
Expected after you enroll in a course
trust_signals.spot: enrolled in the Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate

trust_signals.description: No request for payment or passwords

explanation: Companies often send from subdomains like m.mail.coursera.org. What matters is that the main domain is genuine and nothing sensitive is requested.

subject: Security alert: New sign-in on Windows
body:
Google

New sign-in to your account
ada.okafor@gmail.com

We noticed a new sign-in to your Google Account on a Windows device. If this was you, you don't need to do anything.

If not, we'll help you secure your account.

Check activity

trust_signals.description: Sent from accounts.google.com
Link goes to myaccount.google.com
Says no action is needed if it was you
Gives a web address you can type yourself

explanation: Real security alerts tell you what happened and let you check it yourself. They do not threaten you or ask for your password in the email.

subject: Standup moved to 10:30 tomorrow
body:
Hi team,

Quick heads-up: tomorrow's standup is moving from 9:30 to 10:30 because of the client call. Same Google Meet link as always.

Thanks,
Tolu

trust_signals.description: From a colleague at your own company domain, brightpath.ng
Ordinary request with no pressure
No links, attachments or requests for information

explanation: A routine message from a known colleague on the company domain, asking for nothing.

subject: Booking confirmed – Lagos to Abuja, ref XQ7P2L
body:
Air Peace

Dear Ada Okafor,

trust_signals.description: Comes from flyairpeace.com, Air Peace's real domain
Booking reference and flight details you can verify
Expected after making a booking
Asks for nothing

explanation: A booking confirmation full of verifiable details and no requests is what legitimate transactional mail looks like.

subject: Your Spotify Premium receipt
body:
Spotify

Hi Ada,

Thanks for your payment. Here's your receipt.

Plan: Premium Individual

trust_signals.description: Official spotify.com sender
Matches a subscription you pay for
Only last 4 card digits shown
No link to enter details

explanation: A routine receipt that tells you to manage things on the real website yourself.

subject: Reminder: Course registration closes Friday
body:
University of Ilorin

Dear Student,

This is a reminder that first semester course registration closes on Friday at 11:59 PM.

Please complete your registration on the student portal through the university website. Students who miss the deadline will pay a late registration fee.

Registry Department
University of Ilorin

trust_signals.description: Official .edu.ng university domain
Points you to the official website, no direct link
Deadline is normal academic information, not a threat
Asks for no personal details

explanation: Deadlines alone are not a red flag. This email sends you to a portal you already know rather than to a link it controls.

subject: You appeared in 14 searches this week
body:
LinkedIn

Hi Ada,

You appeared in 14 searches this week. Recruiters from fintech and cybersecurity companies were among those who found you.

See who's searching

Unsubscribe · Help

trust_signals.description: Official linkedin.com sender
Link goes to linkedin.com
Normal engagement email with unsubscribe option

explanation: A typical engagement notification. The link goes to the real domain and nothing is demanded.

subject: GeNS Transaction Notification: Debit ₦12,000
body:
GTBank

If you did not authorise this transaction, please call our contact centre on the number on the back of your card.

trust_signals.description: Official gtbank.com domain
Masked account number
Tells you to call the number on your card, not a number in the email
trust_signals.spot: call our contact centre on the number on the back of your card

trust_signals.description: Reminds you the bank will never ask for your PIN
trust_signals.spot: GTBank will never ask for your PIN, password or token code.

explanation: Transaction alerts are informational. A real one never asks you to click and verify anything.

subject: Your BVN Has Been Suspended – Revalidate Now
body:
Dear Customer,

The Central Bank of Nigeria has SUSPENDED your Bank Verification Number (BVN) because it was not updated. All your bank accounts will be frozen today.

To revalidate, click the link and enter your BVN, date of birth, account number and the OTP sent to your phone.

Revalidate My BVN

This is a final warning. CBN Customer Care Unit.

red_flags.description: The Central Bank does not email individual customers, and never from an @outlook.com address
Threat that every account will be frozen today
red_flags.spot: All your bank accounts will be frozen today.

red_flags.description: Asks for your BVN, account number and OTP, which nobody should ever request
red_flags.spot: enter your BVN, date of birth, account number and the OTP

red_flags.description: Link goes to cbn-bvn-revalidation.com, not cbn.gov.ng

explanation: The CBN regulates banks; it does not contact customers about their BVN. Any message asking for your BVN together with an OTP is trying to take over your account.

subject: CONGRATULATIONS! Your ₦500,000 Loan Is Approved
body:
Dear Customer,

Your loan request of ₦500,000 has been APPROVED with 0% interest for 6 months. No collateral, no BVN check.

To disburse your loan today, pay a refundable insurance fee of ₦8,500 to our account officer below and send the receipt to this email:

Account: 2093847561 – Palmpay – Ibrahim Musa

Your loan will be credited within 30 minutes of confirming the fee. This offer expires in 24 hours.

QuickCredit Disbursement Team

red_flags.description: A lender writing from a free @gmail.com address
You never applied for this loan
You must pay a fee before you can receive the money
red_flags.spot: pay a refundable insurance fee of ₦8,500

red_flags.description: The fee goes to a personal account in an individual's name
0% interest with no checks is too good to be true

explanation: Licensed lenders deduct fees from the loan or add them to repayments; they never ask you to pay first. An upfront "insurance" or "processing" fee is advance-fee fraud.

subject: Wrong Transfer of ₦85,000 Into Your Wallet – Action Needed
body:
Hello Ada,

Due to a system error, ₦85,000 was mistakenly credited into your OPay wallet. To avoid your wallet being restricted, we need to reverse it.

We have sent a 6-digit code to your phone. Please reply to this email with the code so our team can complete the reversal immediately.

Thank you for your cooperation. OPay Reversal Desk

red_flags.description: OPay support writing from a free @gmail.com address
Asks you to send back the code sent to your phone; that code is the key to your account
red_flags.spot: reply to this email with the code

red_flags.description: Threat that your wallet will be restricted
red_flags.spot: To avoid your wallet being restricted

red_flags.description: You can check your own balance in the app: a real wrong transfer is reversed by the company, not by you sharing a code
red_flags.spot: mistakenly credited into your OPay wallet

explanation: The "wrong transfer" story is used to get your one-time code. Never share an OTP with anyone, and check any claimed credit in the official app yourself.

subject: Your WhatsApp Account Will Be Deleted Today
body:
Dear User,

We detected that your WhatsApp account is being used on another phone. To stop your account from being deleted, reply to this email with the 6-digit verification code we just sent by SMS.

If you do not reply within 1 hour, your account, chats and groups will be permanently removed.

WhatsApp Security Team

red_flags.description: WhatsApp support does not email you from a @gmail.com address
Asks for the SMS verification code, which is exactly what someone needs to register your number on their phone
red_flags.spot: 6-digit verification code we just sent by SMS

red_flags.description: One-hour deadline and threat to delete your chats
red_flags.spot: If you do not reply within 1 hour

explanation: Your WhatsApp code is the key to your account. Whoever gets it can take over your number and message your contacts asking for money. Turn on two-step verification in the app.

subject: Final Notice: Your Line Will Be Barred For NIN-SIM Linkage
body:
Attention Subscriber,

Our records show that your phone number is not linked to your National Identification Number (NIN). Your line will be barred within 48 hours.

To link now, fill the form with your NIN, full name, date of birth and a clear photo of your NIN slip, then pay a ₦1,500 linkage fee.

Link My NIN Now

National Identity Management Commission

red_flags.description: A government agency using a free @gmail.com address
Asks for a photo of your NIN slip plus personal details, enough to impersonate you
red_flags.spot: a clear photo of your NIN slip

red_flags.description: Charges a "linkage fee"; linking your NIN to your SIM is done through your network provider
Link goes to nin-sim-linkage-portal.com, not nimc.gov.ng
48-hour threat to bar your line
red_flags.spot: Your line will be barred within 48 hours.

explanation: NIN-SIM linkage is done with your network provider, not through an emailed form. Scammers reuse real government campaigns to collect identity documents.

body:

Keep saving,
The PiggyVest Team

trust_signals.description: Comes from piggyvest.com, PiggyVest's real domain
Only gives information; asks for nothing
Specific Safelock name and dates you can check in the app
No link to log in; it points you to the app
trust_signals.spot: in the PiggyVest app under Safelock

explanation: A normal savings update. It asks you to do nothing and every detail can be checked in the app you already use.

trust_signals.description: Comes from chowdeck.com, the company's real domain
Order number, restaurant and total match what you ordered
Shows only the last 4 digits of the card
Points you to the app for help instead of a link
trust_signals.spot: Open Chowdeck and tap Help on the order.

explanation: A receipt for something you actually ordered. It gives information and asks for nothing.

body:

Please do not use the lifts. The drill should take about 15 minutes.

Thanks,
Facilities Team, BrightPath Technologies

trust_signals.description: Sent from your own company domain, brightpath.ng
Routine information with no link, attachment or request
Nothing to click, pay or log in to

explanation: Not every work email is a trap. This one simply shares information and asks you to do nothing online.

subject: Your September 2026 statement is ready
body:
Kuda.

Kuda

Sends you to the app instead of a link
Reminds you it will never ask for your PIN or OTP
trust_signals.spot: Kuda will never ask for your PIN, password or OTP.

trust_signals.description: No attachment and no urgency
trust_signals.spot: we do not attach statements to emails

explanation: Banks increasingly avoid links and attachments in emails. A message that tells you to open the app yourself is a good sign.

subject: Your Bolt trip on Wednesday evening
body:
Bolt

Thanks for riding with Bolt, Ada.

Pickup: Herbert Macaulay Way, Yaba – 19:42
Drop-off: Admiralty Way, Lekki Phase 1 – 20:31
Driver: Emeka (Toyota Corolla, KJA 412 HB)

Total: ₦7,850 (paid by card ending 4417)

Left something behind? Open the Bolt app, go to Trip history and tap Help.

trust_signals.description: Comes from bolt.eu, Bolt's real domain
Trip details you can match against your own ride
Shows only the last 4 digits of the card
No link to log in; help is in the app
trust_signals.spot: Open the Bolt app, go to Trip history and tap Help.

explanation: A normal trip receipt. If you took the ride, the details will match your trip history.

subject: SMS: account on hold over a BVN mismatch
messages: Dear Customer, your account has been placed on HOLD due to BVN mismatch. Update now to avoid permanent suspension: gtb-bvn-update.xyz

red_flags.description: Banks do not send links asking you to update your BVN
The link goes to gtb-bvn-update.xyz, not gtbank.com
Threat of permanent suspension
The sender name can be faked; it can sit in the same thread as real GTBank alerts

explanation: A sender name like "GTBank" can be faked, so these texts can even appear in the same thread as your real alerts. Banks do not send links to update your BVN; use the official app or visit a branch.

subject: SMS: you won ₦1,000,000 in an MTN promo
messages: MTN MEGA PROMO: Congrats! Your line has won N1,000,000. To claim, send your full name, bank account number and N5,000 activation fee to 08125550193. Hurry, claim closes today!!

red_flags.description: A prize text from an ordinary phone number, not MTN
You never entered any promo
You must pay an "activation fee" to receive a prize
Asks for your bank details
"Claim closes today" pressure

explanation: You cannot win a promo you never entered, and real prizes never cost money to collect. A prize from MTN would not come from an ordinary phone number.

subject: SMS: pay ₦1,200 to redeliver a parcel
messages: GIGL: Your parcel could not be delivered due to incomplete address. Pay N1,200 redelivery fee within 24hrs or it will be returned: gigl-redeliver.top/pay

red_flags.description: Sent from an ordinary phone number
No waybill number or shop name, so it could be sent to anyone
red_flags.spot: Your parcel could not be delivered

red_flags.description: Link goes to gigl-redeliver.top, not giglogistics.com
A small fee makes you less likely to stop and think

explanation: Small "redelivery fees" are a popular way to steal card details. Check deliveries in the courier's app with the waybill number from the shop you ordered from.

subject: SMS: debit alert for a Chowdeck order
messages:
Acct:******4417
DR:NGN5,400.00
Desc:POS/WEB CHOWDECK LAGOS
DT:16-OCT-26 13:47
Bal:NGN181,920.55

trust_signals.description: Matches a payment you just made (the Chowdeck order)
Masked account number and a believable balance
No link, no phone number to call, no request
Only information you can confirm in your banking app

explanation: A normal debit alert: it matches something you just paid for and asks for nothing. Even so, if an alert ever looks wrong, check your balance in the app rather than replying.

subject: SMS: Bolt sign-in code you requested
messages: Your Bolt verification code is 4821. Do not share this code with anyone.

trust_signals.description: You requested it moments ago by signing in
Says plainly not to share the code
trust_signals.spot: Do not share this code with anyone.

trust_signals.description: No link and no request to reply
Short and specific, like real one-time codes

explanation: Genuine, because you just asked for it by signing in. The rule never changes: type the code into the app yourself and never read it out or forward it to anyone.

subject: WhatsApp: earn ₦20,000 a day liking YouTube videos
messages: Hello dear 😊 I am Grace, HR recruiter for an online marketing agency. We need part-time remote staff to like and subscribe to YouTube videos. You earn ₦5,000 to ₦20,000 DAILY.
To start, join our task group and pay a ₦10,000 registration fee (fully refundable after your first task). Interested?

red_flags.description: Message from a number you do not know
red_flags.spot: This number is not saved in your contacts.

red_flags.description: Huge pay for almost no work
You must pay a "registration fee" to get a job
No company name, website or interview

explanation: Task scams start by paying you small amounts for easy work, then ask for bigger "deposits". Real jobs never ask you to pay to start.

subject: WhatsApp: free 50GB data, share to 10 groups
messages:
🎉 AIRTEL 2026 ANNIVERSARY 🎉
Get FREE 50GB data valid for 3 months! Click to claim: airtel-free-data.site
Share this message to 10 groups to activate your bonus.

red_flags.description: Unknown number pretending to be a network
red_flags.spot: This number is not saved in your contacts.

red_flags.description: Link goes to airtel-free-data.site, not an Airtel site
Asks you to share to 10 groups, which spreads the scam
Too-good-to-be-true free data

explanation: Chain messages that make you share to activate a reward spread scam links fast. Network bonuses show up in the official app or by text from the network, not as forwarded links.

subject: WhatsApp: colleague running late to standup
messages: Morning Ada, running about 10 mins late to standup. Traffic on Third Mainland 😩 Start without me, I'll catch up.

trust_signals.description: From a contact saved in your phone
Fits the normal working day (standup at 10:30)
trust_signals.spot: running about 10 mins late to standup

trust_signals.description: No link, money or code requested

explanation: A normal message from a saved colleague. It asks for nothing and matches what you would expect.

subject: WhatsApp: delivery rider at your gate
messages: Good afternoon, I am the Jumia delivery rider for your order JM-284719 (Oraimo FreePods).
I am at the gate of 14 Admiralty Way. Please come out or tell security to let me in. It has already been paid for.

trust_signals.description: Names the exact order you placed and its item
Confirms it is already paid, so there is nothing to pay
trust_signals.spot: It has already been paid for.

trust_signals.description: Asks only for you to come out, no link, code or money
trust_signals.spot: Please come out or tell security to let me in.

trust_signals.description: You are expecting this delivery

explanation: An unknown number is not automatically a scam. This rider names the exact order you are expecting and asks only for you to come to the gate. A scam would ask for a fee, a code or a link.

subject: WhatsApp: your food order is ready for pickup
messages: Hello Ada, your order (2 plates of jollof rice and plantain) is ready for pickup.
Pay at the counter as usual. Thank you!

trust_signals.description: A business number you saved before
Confirms an order you actually placed
trust_signals.spot: your order (2 plates of jollof rice and plantain) is ready for pickup

trust_signals.description: Payment happens in person as usual, not by transfer to a new account
trust_signals.spot: Pay at the counter as usual.

explanation: A small business you already buy from, confirming an order you placed and asking you to pay in person as usual.

subject: CBN Directive: Update your BVN-linked details
body:
Access Bank

Dear Customer,

In line with the recent CBN directive on account verification, all customers are required to re-validate their BVN-linked details by 31 October.

Accounts not updated will be placed on Post-No-Debit restriction.

Update my details

Thank you for banking with us.
Access Bank Plc

Asks you to "Enable Content", which runs the macro
Short, generic reply inserted into a real thread (thread hijacking)

Delivers a code and asks you to share it with no one

Reminds you the bank never asks for your PIN

Dear Ada,

red_flags.description: The From address looks internal, but replies go to brightpath-payroll.com, an outside domain
Payroll already has your bank details; it would not collect them by email
red_flags.spot: your salary bank and account number

red_flags.description: Asks for your BVN in a reply
Threat that your salary will be held
red_flags.spot: may have their salary held until the next cycle

red_flags.description: Borrows a real event (the town hall) to sound genuine
red_flags.spot: As announced at the town hall

explanation: The sender line can be faked, so an internal-looking address proves nothing on its own. The Reply-To is the giveaway here. Confirm payroll changes with HR in person or through the HR system.

red_flags.description: Domain remita-pay.net is not Remita's real remita.net
Urgent "failed payment" with a penalty threat
red_flags.spot: To avoid a late-filing penalty, please retry the payment within 24 hours

red_flags.description: Retry link leads to a payment page outside the real portal
Uses a believable RRR format and real agency names to look routine

explanation: Finance teams receive real Remita receipts, which makes a fake "failed payment" convincing. Check payment status by logging in to remita.net directly, never through an emailed link.

subject: New voice message (0:42) from Adebayo Ogunleye

From: Adebayo Ogunleye (Managing Director)
Length: 0:42

red_flags.description: Domain brightpath-voicemail.com is not brightpath.ng
The "audio" attachment is an .htm web page, not a sound file
Asks you to sign in to Microsoft 365 to hear a voicemail
red_flags.spot: sign in with your Microsoft 365 account

red_flags.description: Uses the MD's name and a late Friday time so you act without checking

explanation: HTML attachments open a fake login page in your browser. A voicemail never needs your password; if the MD really called, ask them directly.

trust_signals.description: Internal brightpath.ng address with no Reply-To mismatch
Points you to the normal ERP workflow, not a new process
States that no bank details have changed
trust_signals.spot: No vendor bank details have changed in this batch.

trust_signals.description: Encourages you to verify by phone, the opposite of a scammer
trust_signals.spot: put the payment on hold and call me

explanation: A finance approval can look like CEO fraud at first glance. The difference: it follows the usual process, changes nothing and invites you to check.

subject: Results of last week's phishing simulation
body:
Hi team,

Last week we sent a simulated phishing email about a "parcel delivery fee" to all staff. Thank you to the 61% of you who reported it.

Your personal result and a 10-minute refresher are on the intranet. Sign in as usual at intranet.brightpath.ng; there is no link in this email on purpose.

Remember: if something feels off, use the Report Phishing button in Outlook.

IT Security, BrightPath Technologies

trust_signals.description: Internal brightpath.ng address with no Reply-To mismatch
No link: tells you to go to the intranet yourself
trust_signals.spot: there is no link in this email on purpose

trust_signals.description: No request for passwords, codes or money
Refers to a real internal process you can confirm with IT
trust_signals.spot: use the Report Phishing button in Outlook

explanation: Security teams run simulations and share results. This one is safe because it asks for nothing and deliberately avoids links.

subject: SMS: mailbox locked in 2 hours, verify now
messages: Microsoft 365: Your BrightPath mailbox will be locked in 2 hours due to a policy violation. Verify your account: m365-login-verify.com/brightpath

red_flags.description: Link goes to m365-login-verify.com, not a Microsoft or brightpath.ng address
Two-hour lock-out threat
Uses your company name to look targeted and real
IT issues would come from your IT team, not an SMS

explanation: Attackers text staff because phones show less of the link and have no email filters. Company account problems are handled by your IT team, not a link in a text.

subject: SMS: "the MD" needs gift cards urgently
messages: Ada, this is Adebayo. I'm in a board meeting and can't talk. I need you to buy 4 Apple gift cards (₦50k each) for a client right away. Send me the codes here, I'll refund you. Keep this between us for now.

red_flags.description: Claims to be the MD but comes from an unknown number
Gift cards are a classic untraceable payment for scammers
Secrecy: "keep this between us"
red_flags.spot: Keep this between us for now.

red_flags.description: Says he cannot talk, so you cannot check
red_flags.spot: I'm in a board meeting and can't talk.

explanation: CEO fraud moves to SMS and WhatsApp to avoid company email checks. Gift cards are untraceable, which is why attackers ask for them. Confirm through a known number or in person.
verify_first: Call the MD on their usual number or ask their office in person. No real request for gift cards arrives by text.

subject: SMS: income tax arrears, pay to avoid penalty
messages: LIRS: Your 2025 personal income tax assessment shows N48,200 outstanding. Pay before 31/10 to avoid penalty and enforcement: lirs-etax.com.ng/pay

red_flags.description: The real LIRS eTax portal is etax.lirs.net, not lirs-etax.com.ng
Penalty and enforcement threat
Most salaried staff pay through PAYE at work, so a personal arrears text is unusual
A sender name like "LIRS" can be faked

explanation: Tax portals do not always end in .gov.ng: the real LIRS eTax portal is etax.lirs.net. Learn the exact address and type it yourself instead of following a texted link.

subject: SMS: code for a ₦289,500 payment you did not make
messages: Your OTP for a NGN289,500.00 payment to an online merchant is 884120. If you did not start this payment, DO NOT share this code. Call the number on the back of your card.

trust_signals.description: Tells you never to share the code
Sends you to the number on the back of your card, not a number in the text
trust_signals.spot: Call the number on the back of your card.

trust_signals.description: No link
Real banks send exactly this kind of code for card payments
trust_signals.spot: Your OTP for a NGN289,500.00 payment to an online merchant is 884120.

explanation: This text is genuine, and it is warning you: someone is trying to use your card. Never share the code, and call your bank using the number on your card to block it. Not every alarming text is a scam.
verify_first: Do not share the code. Call your bank on the number on the back of your card and block the card.

subject: SMS: new debit card ready at your branch
messages: Dear Customer, your new FirstBank debit card ending 2290 has been dispatched to your branch (Yaba). Please pick it up with a valid ID.

trust_signals.description: Matches a card you requested
trust_signals.spot: your new FirstBank debit card ending 2290

trust_signals.description: Collection is in person with ID
trust_signals.spot: Please pick it up with a valid ID.

trust_signals.description: No link, payment or code requested

explanation: A normal service text: no link, no request, and you collect the card in person with ID.

subject: WhatsApp: supplier sends "new" bank details
messages: Good afternoon Ada, this is Chiamaka from Zentrix Supplies. Our email is having issues, so I'm reaching out here.
Please note our NEW account for invoice ZS-2304 (₦1,760,000): 1190027385, Moniepoint MFB, Zentrix Supplies Ltd. Kindly pay today and send the receipt here.

red_flags.description: A number not saved in your contacts, though you already know Chiamaka
red_flags.spot: This number is not saved in your contacts.

red_flags.description: New bank details for an invoice whose email said the details were unchanged
red_flags.spot: Please note our NEW account for invoice ZS-2304

red_flags.description: "Our email is having issues" is a reason to avoid checks
Pressure to pay today

explanation: Payment fraud often moves to WhatsApp so the change avoids the paper trail at work. The invoice really exists, which is what makes this convincing. Call the supplier on the number you already have.
verify_first: Call the supplier on the number already in your records and confirm the account with finance before paying.

subject: WhatsApp: "wrong number" turns into a crypto tip
messages: Hello, is this Mrs Bello? I was told she sells ankara fabrics.
Oh sorry, wrong number! You seem nice though 😊 I'm Linda, I work in crypto trading in London.
I made 40% on USDT this month with a special platform. Would you like me to show you how? Small deposit, big returns.

red_flags.description: A friendly chat with a stranger that turns to money
Promises 40% returns in a month
red_flags.spot: I made 40% on USDT this month

red_flags.description: Pushes a "special platform" you have never heard of
Foreign number with no real connection to you

explanation: A friendly "wrong number" chat that turns into an investment offer is the opening of a long scam: fake profits on a fake platform until you deposit more. Block and do not engage.

subject: WhatsApp: MD thanks you after a meeting
messages: Ada, thanks for the vendor review today.
Let's go through the Zentrix contract renewal at Monday's management meeting. Enjoy your weekend.

trust_signals.description: Saved number for the MD
Refers to a meeting that actually happened
trust_signals.spot: thanks for the vendor review today

trust_signals.description: Moves decisions to a normal meeting, no money or secrecy

explanation: From the MD's saved number, about real work, with no request for money or secrecy. Compare with the gift-card text from an unknown number.

subject: WhatsApp: HR reminder to use the portal
messages: Hi all, reminder that HMO enrolment closes on 25 Oct.
Please choose your plan on the HR portal on the intranet as usual. Don't send ID documents or account details on WhatsApp.

trust_signals.description: Saved HR contact
Matches the HMO renewal email you already received
Sends you to the intranet as usual
trust_signals.spot: choose your plan on the HR portal on the intranet as usual

trust_signals.description: Warns you not to share documents on WhatsApp
trust_signals.spot: Don't send ID documents or account details on WhatsApp.

explanation: A reminder that points you to the usual system and warns against sharing documents on chat, the opposite of what a scammer wants.

subject: WhatsApp: supplier confirms bank details are unchanged
messages: Hi Ada, I've emailed invoice ZS-2304 for the October supplies.
Bank details are unchanged. Call me on my office line if anything ever looks different.

trust_signals.description: Saved contact you already know
Matches the invoice email you received
Bank details explicitly unchanged
Invites you to verify by phone
trust_signals.spot: Call me on my office line if anything ever looks different.

explanation: From the supplier's saved number, matching the invoice email, with unchanged bank details and an invitation to call. This is what a safe supplier message looks like.

Payment by transfer to a personal account; Jumia takes payment at checkout in its app or website

subject: Your end-of-year bonus letter is ready
body:

Threat that your bonus will be cancelled in 24 hours

subject: You have been shortlisted for a ₦500,000 scholarship
body:

Guaranteed award plus a one-day deadline

Google

You have used 13.5 GB of your 15 GB of Google storage (ada.okafor@gmail.com). When it is full, you won't be able to receive new emails in Gmail.

subject: SMS: DStv suspended, renew at a link
messages: DStv: Your subscription has been SUSPENDED due to a billing error. Renew now at 50% discount to restore your channels: dstv-renew.top/pay

red_flags.description: The link goes to dstv-renew.top, not dstv.com
Sudden "suspension" to make you panic
red_flags.spot: SUSPENDED due to a billing error

red_flags.description: A discount to rush you into paying through the link
A sender name like "DStv" can be faked

explanation: Subscription scams copy a real brand's name as the sender and add a discount to rush you. Renew DStv through the MyDStv app, your bank app or USSD, never a texted link.

subject: SMS: airtime recharge confirmed
messages: Y'ello! You have recharged N1,000 airtime. Your main balance is N1,245.50. Thank you for choosing MTN.

trust_signals.description: Matches the airtime you just bought
Only information; no link, number to call or request

explanation: A routine confirmation of something you just did. It asks for nothing and contains no link.

subject: WhatsApp: a Christmas grant you never applied for
messages: 🎄 CONGRATULATIONS! 🎄 Your number has been selected for the 2026 Christmas Empowerment Grant of ₦150,000.
To receive it, fill the form with your name, bank account and BVN: xmas-empowerment-grant.site/apply
Share this message to 5 WhatsApp groups to activate your payment!

red_flags.description: A stranger's number, not saved in your contacts
red_flags.spot: This number is not saved in your contacts.

red_flags.description: A grant you never applied for
Asks for your bank account and BVN on an unknown site
Sharing to groups spreads the scam to your friends
red_flags.spot: Share this message to 5 WhatsApp groups

explanation: Fake grants spread on WhatsApp by asking people to share them. The form collects bank details and BVNs for fraud, and the "share to activate" step makes your friends the next targets.
